key_insight: TACO proposes a memory-efficient optimizer for LLM fine-tuning that aims to preserve AdamW-like behavior while dramatically reducing optimizer-state overhead. The core idea is to use ternary, absolute-max, column-wise one-sparse updates to make full-parameter fine-tuning fit better on modern GPUs.
problem_solved: Full-parameter LLM fine-tuning is often limited by the large memory footprint of optimizer states, which can prevent larger models from fitting on available GPUs. Existing memory-saving methods either compress state, drop first-order gradients, or change the update geometry in ways that can hurt fine-tuning quality.
method: Uses ternary update values to reduce optimizer-state complexity.
Applies absolute-max, column-wise one-sparse updates to lower memory usage while keeping updates efficient.
Targets AdamW-style fine-tuning behavior more closely than matrix-update approaches like Muon.
impact: This matters because it can enable larger-model fine-tuning on the same hardware, reducing memory bottlenecks and infrastructure cost. Practitioners may get a more practical optimizer that balances efficiency with strong fine-tuning performance.
